answer: In an agent economy, each identity must lock a refundable stake and periodically answer unpredictable, cross-checked tasks from established peers; peers who detect duplicated control or coordinated false reports can challenge it, and an adjudicator slashes the stake. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund every fake identity and risk losing capital when its onyx, grove, and dune accounts reveal correlated behavior, making mass imitation expensive even when software is cheap.
